items.heading: People Often Ask
items.text: People often ask for a humanities jobs list with a salary next to each role. A single table of numbers for these lanes would be misleading, because pay in content, research, policy, communication and learning design swings widely with the employer type, the city, the seniority and the skill layer you add. A small agency, a large company and a research organisation can pay very differently for the same job title.

items.heading: Search By the Role Title,
items.text: Search by the role title, not the stream. Look up 'UX researcher', 'content strategist' or 'policy analyst' on current job postings and salary-tracking sites, then compare entry-level and experienced listings separately.

items.heading: Compare Like with Like
items.text: Compare like with like. Use the same city and a similar company type before you trust any average.

items.heading: Ask What Raised the Pay
items.text: Ask what raised the pay. In the lanes above, the ceiling usually rises with proof of work and a use skill such as research methods, analytics or SEO, not with the degree name.
